questions.stem: On complete hydrogenation, natural rubber produces
questions.solution: Natural rubber is cis-1,4-polyisoprene with the repeat unit –CH₂–C(CH₃)=CH–CH₂–. Saturating the C=C gives –CH₂–CH(CH₃)–CH₂–CH₂–. This repeat unit is one propylene unit (–CH₂–CH(CH₃)–) joined to one ethylene unit (–CH₂–CH₂–), so the product is an alternating ethylene–propylene copolymer. Vulcanisation is cross-linking with sulfur, not hydrogenation.

check.note: Two independent solutions agree; matches the official key printed in the paper (A)

questions.stem: Positive Tollen's test is observed for
questions.solution: Tollens' reagent is reduced to silver by aldehydes and by α-hydroxy ketones. Acrolein (A) and benzaldehyde (B) are aldehydes and both give a silver mirror. Benzoin (C) is an α-hydroxy ketone: in the basic ammoniacal medium it is readily oxidised (via its enediol) to benzil, so it also tests positive. Chalcone (D) is a simple α,β-unsaturated ketone with no aldehyde or α-hydroxy group, so it does not react.

check.note: Two independent solutions agree; matches the official key printed in the paper (A, B, C)

questions.stem:
The product(s) of the following reaction sequence is(are)
Aniline —i) Acetic anhydride/pyridine ii) KBrO₃/HBr iii) H₃O⁺, heat iv) NaNO₂/HCl, 273–278 K v) Cu/HBr→ ?
questions.solution: Acetylation converts aniline into acetanilide, which moderates the activation and so prevents polybromination. Br₂ generated from KBrO₃/HBr then monobrominates acetanilide at the less hindered para position. Acid hydrolysis gives 4-bromoaniline, and diazotisation followed by Cu/HBr (Gattermann/Sandmeyer) replaces N₂⁺ by Br. The product is 1,4-dibromobenzene.

check.note: Two independent solutions agree; matches the official key printed in the paper (B)

questions.stem:
The correct statement(s) about the following reaction sequence is(are)
Cumene (C₉H₁₂) —i) O₂ ii) H₃O⁺→ P —CHCl₃/NaOH→ Q (major) + R (minor)
Q —NaOH, PhCH₂Br→ S

options.text: Q gives dark violet coloration with 1% aqueous FeCl₃ solution
S gives dark violet coloration with 1% aqueous FeCl₃ solution

questions.solution: Cumene is oxidised to its hydroperoxide, which is cleaved by acid to phenol (P) and acetone. The Reimer–Tiemann reaction on phenol gives salicylaldehyde (Q, ortho, major) and 4-hydroxybenzaldehyde (R, para, minor). R forms intermolecular hydrogen bonds, so it is not steam volatile, unlike Q with its intramolecular hydrogen bond. Q has a free phenolic OH and gives the violet FeCl₃ colour. Benzylating Q gives 2-(benzyloxy)benzaldehyde (S), which still has a CHO group (positive 2,4-DNP test) but no phenolic OH, so it gives no FeCl₃ colour.

check.note: Two independent solutions agree; matches the official key printed in the paper (B, C)

questions.stem:
In the following monobromination reaction, the number of possible chiral products is
(R)-2-bromopentane (1.0 mole, enantiomerically pure; drawn as a Fischer projection) —Br₂ (1.0 mole), 300 °C→ ?
questions.solution: Radical bromination can replace H at C-1, C-2, C-3, C-4 or C-5, and the original stereocentre is untouched unless C-2 itself reacts. C-1 gives 1,2-dibromopentane (one chiral product), and C-2 gives achiral 2,2-dibromopentane. C-3 creates a new stereocentre and gives two diastereomers of 2,3-dibromopentane, both chiral. C-4 gives (2R,4R)-2,4-dibromopentane (chiral) and the meso (2R,4S) isomer (achiral). C-5 gives chiral 1,4-dibromopentane, so the total is 1 + 2 + 1 + 1 = 5.

check.note: Two independent solutions agree; matches the official key printed in the paper (5)
